inputs.original_proposal: Review: coalesced signal updates with LiveView Page v0.3.0 phase 2

blockers: Thread safety violation in qttunebridge.cpp:212-220 - m_currentFrameCount is accessed non-atomically in onFrame() worker thread, then incremented non-atomically in handleFrameInternal() GUI thread. The check 'if (self->m_currentFrameCount >= FrameListModel::MaxFrames)' races with the '++m_currentFrameCount' increment, creating a TOCTOU race condition.
Thread safety violation in qttunebridge.cpp:245 - The m_currentFrameCount increment in handleFrameInternal() is not atomic, allowing data races when multiple frames arrive concurrently.
questions: Why was the entire SignalListModel and signal batching infrastructure removed? The old code had hardcoded 8-byte buffer assumptions in qttune_decode_signal() which was incorrect for CAN-FD; was this intentional simplification or loss of functionality?

What is the intended backpressure strategy now? The old code used atomic m_inFlightFrames with MaxInFlightFrames=1000 to bound queued work; the new code relies on m_currentFrameCount which is not atomic and provides weaker guarantees.
nits: Removed forceFrameCountForTesting() test helper eliminated the ability to verify boundary conditions at MaxFrames=10000
Removed StreamingContinuesPastTenThousandFrames test means no verification that the new non-atomic counter approach handles the 10k frame boundary correctly
Comment in qttunebridge.cpp:86 states 'frame is stack-owned by mock_worker' but this lifetime guarantee must hold for any real transport implementation
Removed signalBatchCount property and related batching metrics eliminate observability into signal update throughput
